newsitem.title: UK: NatPower sees "slight" fall in market share.
newsitem.headline: NatPower sees "slight" fall in market share.

text.p: British electricity generator National Power said on Wednesday it expected to see a slight fall in market share this year from levels of 24 percent last year.
"There will be a slight decline of market share this year," finance director Roger Witcomb told an analysts' meeting after annual results.
National Power saw year pre-tax profits before exceptional items slip eight percent to 740 million stg and paid out a dividend of 25 pence, up from 23 pence a year ago.
"The amount of new plant coming on this year is less than it was last year, so we would expect a much smaller decline in that part of our output than this year," he added.
Market share last year fell to 24 percent from 32 percent, but Witcomb pointed out that over half of that drop was due to divestment of some plant.
National Power executives added that wholesale costs appeared to have stopped slipping and "if anything, prices are up," one executive added.
Witcomb added that current uncertainties made the company reluctant to return cash to shareholders.

"Given the uncertainties that are around, both...the opportunities that are there (for investment) in the international business...and other uncertainties...which would make us reluctant, I think, to contemplate returning cash to shareholders at this very minute," Witcomb said.
National Power paid out a hefty one pound per share special dividend at results last year but this year trimmed it back.

It has said it does not think it should be targeted by a one-off windfall tax proposed by the new Labour government on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities, details of which have not yet been announced.

This year's dividend increase of around nine percent in real growth was "clearly an indication that we won't be going back to 49 percent increases and the (special) dividend that we gave last year," Witcomb said.

He said the company was committed to maintaining real dividend growth and added that, "We have said in the past that for short periods we'd be prepared to go down as low as 1.5 (times)," for dividend cover, which is currently at two times.
